items.mainDefect: Google updateEvent uses a fallback predicate that cannot match when externalCalendarId is missing, leaving calendarId undefined.

secondary.defect: Google deleteEvent uses the same invalid fallback, causing deletion to target the primary calendar instead of the destination calendar.

items.mainDefect: Recurring-event deletion runs again for each outer calendar reference, redundantly deleting the same events.

secondary.defect: Recurring-event deletion selects only the first calendar reference of each booking, leaving other hosts' calendar events undeleted.

items.mainDefect: Google updateEvent cannot resolve the destination calendar when externalCalendarId is missing because its fallback compares against that missing value.

secondary.defect: Google deleteEvent also compares destination calendar IDs against a missing externalCalendarId, preventing deletion from the intended calendar.

items.mainDefect: Office365 uses the first destination calendar's externalId regardless of the executing credential, causing team-member events to target the wrong calendar.

secondary.defect: Lark also uses the first destination calendar instead of the destination belonging to the executing credential.
The CalDAV base service also uses the first destination calendar instead of the destination belonging to the executing credential.

items.mainDefect: Google updateEvent's fallback compares calendar IDs against a falsy externalCalendarId, producing an undefined calendarId.

secondary.defect: Google deleteEvent has the same dead fallback predicate, silently retargeting deletion to the primary calendar.
